domain_entities.name: ApprovalsQueueItem
attributes: employeeName: string | null (derived; may be absent from API response)
status: LeaveStatus (always SUBMITTED while in queue)
domain_entities.purpose: Read-model projection of a LeaveRequest awaiting the signed-in manager/admin's decision. It is a derived view, not a persisted entity: membership is computed from LeaveRequest.status === SUBMITTED and the viewer's role/ownership.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Existing source-of-truth entity. The approvals queue is a filtered projection of SUBMITTED requests not raised by the viewer; a decision (approve/reject) transitions status out of SUBMITTED, which removes the request from the queue.

domain_entities.name: EmployeeProfile
domain_entities.purpose: The signed-in viewer's identity and role, fetched via GET /employees/me (never decoded from the JWT in the browser). role is the sole driver of queue visibility and link/route gating.

business_rules: Queue membership: a LeaveRequest appears in the approvals queue iff status === SUBMITTED AND employeeId !== viewer.id AND viewer.role ∈ {MANAGER, ADMIN}. The backend GET /leaves already scopes results by role (MANAGER receives direct reports' requests); the queue applies the additional SUBMITTED + not-self filters client-side. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever ApprovalsQueueItem membership appears, not only here]

Queue visibility is role-gated: only MANAGER or ADMIN may view the approvals queue. An EMPLOYEE must neither see the dashboard link nor be able to reach the route; the guard is enforced at the route boundary (not only on the link), so direct navigation as an EMPLOYEE shows no other employee's data. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever ApprovalsQueue access appears, not only here]

Decision authority is the single existing matrix in getAvailableLeaveActions(status, role, isOwner): approve/reject are available only for a SUBMITTED request by a MANAGER or ADMIN who is not the owner. The queue must reuse this helper — never a second copy of the status+role+ownership rule. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest decision authority appears, not only here]

A decision (approve or reject) transitions the request out of SUBMITTED (to APPROVED or REJECTED), which removes it from the queue. The queue reflects the new status or drops the row without a manual reload. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever ApprovalsQueueItem lifecycle appears, not only here]
The empty queue ("nothing waiting on you") is a normal, non-error, non-loading condition and must be rendered as an explicit empty state distinct from both the loading state and the error state.

Role is derived solely from the EmployeeProfile returned by GET /employees/me; the JWT is never decoded in the browser to determine what to show or allow. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever EmployeeProfile.role appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
Domain slice for the manager approvals queue (web-only). No new persisted entities: the queue is a derived read-model projection (ApprovalsQueueItem) over the existing LeaveRequest entity, filtered to status === SUBMITTED, employeeId !== viewer.id, and viewer.role ∈ {MANAGER, ADMIN}. The viewer's identity/role comes from EmployeeProfile (GET /employees/me), never from decoding the JWT in the browser.

Lifecycle states introduced: ApprovalsQueueItem has AWAITING_DECISION → RESOLVED (a decision transitions the underlying LeaveRequest out of SUBMITTED, removing it from the queue). LeaveRequest's existing lifecycle (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) is unchanged and is the source of the queue's membership.

Binding business rules (broad): queue membership predicate; role-gated visibility enforced at the route boundary (not only the link); decision authority reuses the single getAvailableLeaveActions matrix (no second copy); a decision removes the row without manual reload; role derived only from EmployeeProfile. Narrow rule: the empty queue is a distinct normal state, not loading/error.

Open question: the API exposes employeeId but no employee name and the web employee service only has getMe(), so how the "employee" column is rendered is undecided (render id vs omit vs resolve from an existing list — none currently exists).

open_questions.question: The API's LeaveRequestView exposes employeeId but no employee name, and the web employee service only exposes getMe() (no direct-report name lookup). The feature asks the queue to show "employee" — how should the employee column be rendered when only employeeId is available?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the queue shows a human-readable employee identifier or a raw id. Constraint forbids adding endpoints, so the options are constrained to what the existing API returns.
candidate_options: Omit the employee column and rely on the detail-page link for identity
Resolve names client-side from an existing list endpoint if one is already fetched (none currently exists in web)
